description:
FILED s473t5b (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 3 (op/ CHECK 2): 44 of
t/op/heredoc.t's blessed fail rows, every one of its `Eval'd Indented
here-doc:` cluster.

REPRODUCER (valid perl; PCL fails it in FILE mode too, so the string eval is
not the point):

    $_ = "";
    s//<<~EOF.""/e; print
        some data
        EOF

  perl:  some data
  PCL:   Undefined subroutine &main::EOF called

The here-doc OPENER sits inside the `s///e` REPLACEMENT, and its BODY lies
after the statement -- which is where perl puts it, because the replacement is
compiled as code while the body follows the statement.  PPI does not support
this at all; its own TO DO list says so ("Add support for here-doc in
s///e"), and the effect is that the body and its terminator are left as loose
CODE, so `EOF` becomes a bareword call and the body text becomes statements.

PCL ALREADY HAS THE WORKAROUND FOR THE SIBLING SHAPE, and it is one function:
`Pl::ExprToCL::_splice_interp_heredocs` (s356-era, for t/base/lex.t's
`s|(?:)|"${\<<END}" â¦ |e`).  It scans the text it is handed for a `<<TAG`
opener, finds the terminator line, hoists the body into a `my $__pcl_hd_N`
and replaces the opener with that variable.  It cannot help here because it is
handed the REPLACEMENT TEXT only (`<<~EOF.""`), and the body is not in it.

WHAT THE FIX NEEDS: the enclosing statement's source, not just the
replacement.  Two shapes to keep in mind:
  * FILE mode -- PPI hands over a `PPI::Token::Regexp::Substitute` whose
    following siblings are the body lines mis-lexed as code; the body is
    recoverable from the document (or from the source text plus the token's
    line_number) and the loose statements must be DELETED, not just ignored.
  * STRING EVAL -- the whole text including the body is one string, so the
    existing splicer would work if it were run over the WHOLE eval text
    before parsing rather than over the replacement.

ALSO BROKEN IN THE SAME FUNCTION, and worth fixing with it (rule 11: it is a
SECOND COPY of the indentation rule the s473t5b repair just fixed in
`Pl::Parser`): `_splice_interp_heredocs` computes a `<<~` indent as the
MINIMUM indentation over the body and the terminator line, where perl's rule
is the whitespace before the DELIMITER TEXT on the terminator line; and it
matches the terminator with `s/^\s+//` + string equality, which cannot match a
delimiter that itself begins with whitespace (`<<~' EOF'`).  Both diverge from
`Pl::Parser::_repair_indented_heredocs`, which is now the one correct reading
of that rule -- when this task lands, the two should share it.

MEASURED COST: 44 rows of t/op/heredoc.t (`Eval'd Indented here-doc: <<~...`,
every delimiter spelling x two script-end variants).  The file is DIFF 52/86
after the s473t5b fix; these 44 are the biggest remaining cluster, and the
other 42 are perl's diagnostics for INVALID here-doc source (principle 9).

BAR: the reproducer above plus the file's 24 delimiter spellings, perl as the
oracle; t/op/heredoc.t re-run and its rows spliced; the shared indentation
reading proved by both guards (`Pl/t/heredoc-indent-01.t` must stay green).
subject: a here-doc OPENED INSIDE an s///e replacement whose BODY lies outside the replacement text: PPI leaves the body as loose code (its own TO DO says here-doc-in-s///e is unsupported) and the terminator becomes a bareword call -- 44 rows of t/op/heredoc.t
